bib.title: SELF-RAG: LEARNING TO RETRIEVE, GENERATE, AND CRITIQUE THROUGH SELF-REFLECTION

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; appendix prompt tables 8-12 read in part (instructions and first demonstrations).

question: Can a single LM be trained to decide when to retrieve, and to critique retrieved passages and its own output, so that factuality and citation accuracy improve without losing versatility?
hypothesis: Indiscriminate fixed-number retrieval hurts versatility and quality; training an LM to emit reflection tokens and using them at decoding gives better quality, factuality and attribution than standard RAG.
contributions: SELF-RAG framework: one LM trained with reflection tokens to retrieve on demand, generate and critique
Critic model distilled from GPT-4 labels inserts reflection tokens offline, so no critic is needed at training or inference
Inference-time customisation via segment-level beam search weighted by reflection-token probabilities and retrieval threshold
Outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on several tasks, with higher citation precision on ASQA

method.summary: Llama 2 7B/13B generators are fine-tuned with the standard next-token loss on instruction data whose outputs are augmented offline by a Llama2-7B critic with Retrieve, IsRel, IsSup, IsUse tokens and inserted passages. At inference the model predicts a Retrieve token, processes K passages in parallel and picks segments by beam search over a weighted sum of critique-token scores.
method.task: retrieval-augmented generation: short-form QA, closed-set classification, long-form generation with citations

training.objective: standard next-token log-likelihood on output plus reflection tokens (Eq. 2); critic: conditional LM likelihood of reflection tokens (Eq. 1)

inference.decoding: segment-level beam search, beam width 2; greedy at token level; one sentence = one segment; vllm
inference.max_tokens: 100 new tokens open-domain QA and ALCE; 50 for PubHealth/ARC-C; FactScore 500 for baselines, 200 per segment for SELF-RAG
inference.samples: single run per item; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot, task instruction only (Table 5); no instruction for open-domain QA
inference.retrieval: Contriever-MS MARCO, top 5 (up to ten documents stated in 4.3); 2018 Wikipedia embeddings, Dec 2020 corpus for PopQA; bio and open-domain QA add 5 Google Programmable Search documents; ASQA uses provided GTR-XXL top 5

prompts.text: Given an instruction, please make a judgment on whether finding some external documents from the web (e.g., Wikipedia) helps to generate a better response. Please answer [Yes] or [No] and write an explanation.
Is the following statement correct or not? Say true if it's correct; otherwise, say false. Don't capitalize or add periods, just say "true" or "false".
Tell me a bio about [Person Name]

limits: Authors keep training data to 150k and say more data may help; scale curves still rising.
Off-the-shelf retrievers trained on knowledge-intensive tasks are weak for open-ended generation; joint retriever training left for future work.
Output can still be not fully supported by citations (Ethical Concerns).
SELF-RAG 7B sometimes beats 13B on factual precision because it writes shorter outputs.
Toolformer, SAIL, CoVE numbers are reported from their papers, not re-run.
Ablations use 50k training instances and 150 ASQA samples; no seeds or significance tests stated.
Optimizer, seeds and ARC/PubHealth/Bio/ASQA test sizes not stated.
